### Summary

A few radiative-transfer problems have an exact answer that needs no solver: a beam crossing an absorbing slab, a
slab that only emits, and the bookkeeping of energy between the top, the column and the surface. This section runs
both solvers (`solver: toon` and `solver: disort`) on those problems. They check the parts of each solver that do
not depend on the scattering approximation, and they confirm that the DISORT reference of @sec-ch05-reference is
right where an exact answer exists.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Closed forms @eq-ch05-analytic-beam, @eq-ch05-analytic-e3; closure @eq-ch05-analytic-closure.

**Data.** Fluxes at every level of single- and multi-layer slabs, normalised by $F_{\mathrm{inc}}$.

**Placement.** A measurement on the solvers; nothing in pyharp runs it.

**Activation.** `solver` in the band YAML (`toon` or `disort`); required, no default.

**Guarantee / limits.** Beam to $2\times10^{-16}$; Toon emission to $3.2\times10^{-4}$.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer below.
:::

Local symbols: $A_{\mathrm{col}}$ the flux absorbed in the column [$\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$]; $I_s$ the radiance
leaving a Lambertian surface [$\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}\,sr^{-1}}$]; $E_3$ the third
exponential integral, $E_3(x) = \int_0^1 \mu\, e^{-x/\mu}\,\mathrm{d}\mu$ [-]; $F_{\mathrm{net}}$, $J$, $A_s$ as
in the ch2 notation; $F_{\mathrm{inc}}$ as in @eq-ch05-reference-finc.

### Derivation

**A beam in an absorbing slab.** With no scattering ($\omega = 0$) the beam loses energy along its path only. A
beam of flux $F_0$ normal to its direction, entering at $\tau = 0$ with cosine $\mu_0$, keeps the fraction
$e^{-\tau/\mu_0}$ after the slant path $\tau/\mu_0$, so the downward flux on a horizontal surface is

$$
F_{\mathrm{dir}}(\tau) = \mu_0 F_0\, e^{-\tau/\mu_0} ,
$$ {#eq-ch05-analytic-beam}
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch05-analytic-beam check_ch05_analytic.py [C1] -->

with $\tau$ [-] the optical depth measured down from the top, and no diffuse flux arises. Toon's shortwave kernel
computes @eq-ch05-analytic-beam directly when every layer has $\omega \le 10^{-12}$ and the surface is black (the
branch on `all_zero_w` in `toon_mckay89_shortwave`,
{{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89_shortwave_impl.h toon_mckay89_shortwave repo=pyharp >}}).

**The beam reflected by a Lambertian surface.** A surface of albedo $A_s$ [-] at $\tau_0$ reflects the flux
$A_s F_{\mathrm{dir}}(\tau_0)$ isotropically, with radiance $I_s = A_s F_{\mathrm{dir}}(\tau_0)/\pi$. Through an
absorbing path of vertical optical depth $\tau_0 - \tau$ the radiance in direction $\mu$ keeps
$e^{-(\tau_0-\tau)/\mu}$, so the
upward flux at $\tau$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}
F^{+}(\tau) &= 2\pi \int_0^1 I_s\, e^{-(\tau_0-\tau)/\mu}\, \mu\,\mathrm{d}\mu \\
            &= 2\pi I_s\, E_3(\tau_0 - \tau) \\
            &= 2 A_s F_{\mathrm{dir}}(\tau_0)\, E_3(\tau_0 - \tau) .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-analytic-reflect}
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch05-analytic-reflect check_ch05_analytic.py [C14] -->

**A slab that only emits.** An isothermal slab of optical depth $\tau_0$, Planck radiance $B$ and no scattering,
with no radiation entering at the top, sends down along $\mu$ the radiance
$I^{-}(\tau_0,\mu) = B\,(1 - e^{-\tau_0/\mu})$. The downward flux at its bottom is

$$
\begin{aligned}
F^{-}(\tau_0) &= 2\pi \int_0^1 B\,(1 - e^{-\tau_0/\mu})\, \mu\,\mathrm{d}\mu \\
              &= \pi B - 2\pi B\, E_3(\tau_0) \\
              &= \pi B\,\bigl(1 - 2E_3(\tau_0)\bigr) .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-analytic-e3}
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch05-analytic-e3 check_ch05_analytic.py [C21] -->

Over a black surface at the same temperature the column is in equilibrium and the upward flux is $\pi B$ at every
level. Toon's thermal kernel integrates over $\mu$ with five Gauss points (`uarr`, `wuarr` in
`toon_mckay89_longwave`, {{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89_longwave_impl.h toon_mckay89_longwave repo=pyharp >}}), so
@eq-ch05-analytic-e3 measures that quadrature.

**Energy closure.** Write the net flux upward-positive, $F_{\mathrm{net}} = F^{+} - F^{-} - F_{\mathrm{dir}}$
[$\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$], and $J$ [$\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}\,sr^{-1}}$] for the mean radiance including the beam. Integrating
the radiative-transfer equation over all directions gives the divergence of the net flux, and integrating that over
the column gives the absorbed flux:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\mathrm{d}F_{\mathrm{net}}}{\mathrm{d}\tau} &= (1-\omega)\, 4\pi J \\
A_{\mathrm{col}} &= F_{\mathrm{net}}(\tau_0) - F_{\mathrm{net}}(0) = \int_0^{\tau_0} (1-\omega)\, 4\pi J\,\mathrm{d}\tau .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch05-analytic-closure}
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch05-analytic-closure check_ch05_analytic.py [C25] -->

Two consequences are checked. With $\omega = 1$ the right side vanishes, so $F_{\mathrm{net}}$ is the same at every
level. With $\omega < 1$, the flux drop $F_{\mathrm{net}}(\tau_0) - F_{\mathrm{net}}(0)$ and the integral of the
mean radiance are two independent routes to $A_{\mathrm{col}}$. A third line, reflected plus column-absorbed plus
surface-absorbed equal to incident, is an identity of these definitions once the top boundary has
$F^{-}(0) = 0$ and $F_{\mathrm{dir}}(0) = \mu_0 F_0$; it therefore checks that boundary condition. The surface itself
must satisfy $F^{+}(\tau_0) = A_s\,\bigl(F^{-}(\tau_0) + F_{\mathrm{dir}}(\tau_0)\bigr)$.

Every expression above is exact; nothing in this section is truncated except the solvers' own discretisations,
which are what the comparison measures. The check is `check_ch05_analytic.py` (Tests layer).

### Numerical method

The beam cases use five layers of thickness fractions 0.1, 0.3, 0.05, 0.25 and 0.3 of
$\tau_0 \in \{0.01, 0.1, 1, 3, 10, 30\}$, at $\mu_0 \in \{0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1\}$, with $A_s = 0$ and $0.4$. The
emitting slab has five equal layers, $\tau_0 \in \{0.01, 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, 10\}$, $T = 250$ K, the band 500 to
1000 $\mathrm{cm^{-1}}$; Toon runs with `hard_surface`, so its surface emits $(1 - A_s)\,\pi B$ at the bottom-level
temperature, as DISORT's does. The closure cases are 72 slabs of 400 equal layers for DISORT (32 streams) and of 10
layers for Toon, $\tau_0 \in \{0.1, 1, 10\}$, $\omega \in \{0.3, 0.9, 1\}$, $g \in \{0, 0.85\}$,
$\mu_0 \in \{0.2, 1\}$, $A_s \in \{0, 0.4\}$. DISORT's mean radiance comes from `gather_flx`
({{< code src/disort.cpp DisortImpl::gather_flx repo=pydisort >}}), channel 4, and the integral of
@eq-ch05-analytic-closure is taken by Simpson's rule over the 401 levels.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch05-analytic-e3
#| fig-cap: "Error of the downward flux at the bottom of a grey isothermal slab against the closed form, divided by pi B, against the slab optical depth: Toon (green squares, solid) and DISORT with 4 (vermillion down-triangles, dashed), 16 (orange up-triangles, dash-dot) and 64 streams (blue circles, dotted). Toon's five-point quadrature stays within 3.2e-4; DISORT needs 16 streams to match it and reaches a floor of 7.4e-7, the difference between its band Planck integral and pyharp's."
#| fig-alt: "Log-log plot of error against optical depth from 0.01 to 10. Toon's error is about 1e-4 for thin slabs and falls to 1e-9 for thick ones. DISORT with 4 streams has errors up to 1e-2, with 16 streams up to 6e-5, and with 64 streams about 1e-7 rising to a flat 7e-7."
#| echo: false
from pyharp_report.ch05.figures.fig_analytic_e3 import make_fig
make_fig()
```

@fig-ch05-analytic-e3 shows the error of @eq-ch05-analytic-e3 for both solvers.

### Code

@tbl-ch05-analytic-code lists the code each analytic case exercises.

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| shortwave kernel, pure-absorption branch | {{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89_shortwave_impl.h toon_mckay89_shortwave repo=pyharp >}} | `toon_mckay89_shortwave` | `solver: toon` |
| thermal kernel, five-point quadrature | {{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89_longwave_impl.h toon_mckay89_longwave repo=pyharp >}} | `toon_mckay89_longwave` | `flags: planck` |
| surface emission $(1 - A_s)\pi B$ | {{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89.hpp ToonMcKay89OptionsImpl::hard_surface repo=pyharp >}} | `hard_surface` | `hard_surface` flag |
| band Planck radiance | {{< code src/radiation/bbflux.cpp bbflux_wavenumber overload=3 repo=pyharp >}} | `bbflux_wavenumber` | always |
| DISORT fluxes and mean radiance | {{< code src/disort.cpp DisortImpl::gather_flx repo=pydisort >}} | `gather_flx` | `solver: disort` |
| layer cut-off | {{< code cdisort213/cdisort.c c_disort_set repo=pydisort >}} | `c_disort_set` | multi-layer beam runs |

: Code map of the analytic cases. {#tbl-ch05-analytic-code}

1. Toon's shortwave kernel tests every layer's $\omega$ against $10^{-12}$ and the surface albedo against
   $10^{-12}$; when all pass it sets the downward flux to @eq-ch05-analytic-beam and the upward flux to zero
   (`all_zero_w` in {{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89_shortwave_impl.h toon_mckay89_shortwave repo=pyharp >}}). Otherwise the
   general two-stream solve of @sec-ch05-toon-accuracy runs, also for $\omega = 0$ over a reflecting surface.
2. Toon's thermal kernel takes the band Planck radiance $B$ from `bbflux_wavenumber`
   ({{< code src/radiation/bbflux.cpp bbflux_wavenumber overload=3 repo=pyharp >}}). That function returns a radiance
   [$\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}\,sr^{-1}}$], not a flux; the flux of a black surface is $\pi$ times it.
3. Without `hard_surface` the thermal kernel's surface source is $B + B_1/2$, with $B_1$ the Planck gradient of the
   bottom layer, not $(1 - A_s)B$ (`bsurf_flux` in
   {{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89_longwave_impl.h toon_mckay89_longwave repo=pyharp >}}); the comparisons here set
   `hard_surface` so both solvers have the same boundary.

### Tests

@tbl-ch05-analytic-tests lists the checks of this section.

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `check_ch05_analytic.py` [C1], [C4], [C6], [C11] | @eq-ch05-analytic-beam, both solvers, $A_s = 0$ and $0.4$ | $10^{-12}$ relative | a few hundred roundings of one exponential in double |
| `check_ch05_analytic.py` [C3], [C10], [C13] | DISORT below absorption depth 10 | $e^{-10}$, $A_s e^{-10}$ | the largest beam `lyrcut` can drop |
| `check_ch05_analytic.py` [C14] | @eq-ch05-analytic-reflect, DISORT 64 streams | $10^{-4}$ | the quadrature error of @fig-ch05-analytic-e3 at 16 streams |
| `check_ch05_analytic.py` [C21] | @eq-ch05-analytic-e3, DISORT 64 streams | $10^{-4}$ | same |
| `check_ch05_analytic.py` [C23], [C25] | @eq-ch05-analytic-closure, DISORT | $10^{-6}$, $10^{-4}$ | Simpson's rule on 400 layers, error of order $h^4$ |
| `tests/test_toon.py` (pytest) | `test_toon_sw_pure_absorption`: Toon against @eq-ch05-analytic-beam | $10^{-8}$ absolute | not stated in the test |

: Tests of the analytic cases. {#tbl-ch05-analytic-tests}

Both solvers reproduce @eq-ch05-analytic-beam to $1.93\times10^{-16}$ relative, return an upward flux of exactly
zero over a black surface, and keep the surface balance to $6.9\times10^{-18}$ (Toon) and $1.7\times10^{-14}$
(DISORT) of the incident flux. DISORT reproduces @eq-ch05-analytic-reflect to $4.8\times10^{-8}$; Toon misses it by
$6.25\times10^{-3}$, because it carries the reflected field with two streams.[^ch05-ana-run]

For the emitting slab, Toon's error against @eq-ch05-analytic-e3 is $-3.2\times10^{-4}$ of $\pi B$ at
$\tau_0 = 0.01$ and falls below $10^{-8}$ for $\tau_0 \ge 3$. DISORT's largest error is $9.8\times10^{-3}$ at
4 streams, $6.1\times10^{-5}$ at 16 and $7.4\times10^{-7}$ at 64. Both give the equilibrium flux over a black
surface, Toon to round-off and DISORT to $7.4\times10^{-7}$.[^ch05-ana-run]

Closure, DISORT: the net flux of the $\omega = 1$ slabs is constant to $1.5\times10^{-7}$ of the incident flux;
the two routes to $A_{\mathrm{col}}$ agree to $4.9\times10^{-5}$; the top boundary condition holds to
$7.2\times10^{-10}$ and the surface balance to $6.8\times10^{-10}$. Toon: the surface balance holds to
$5.4\times10^{-11}$ and $A_{\mathrm{col}} \ge 0$ in every slab with $\omega < 1$.[^ch05-ana-run]

All of these run on the CPU in double precision.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- **Toon with $\omega = 1$ exactly.** The net flux is constant, as closure requires, but because the solution is
  wrong everywhere: the upward and downward fluxes are equal at every level. The reflectance differs from the
  $\omega = 1 - 10^{-12}$ run by up to 0.997 of the incident flux. This is the defect of
  @sec-ch05-toon-accuracy, Limits.[^ch05-ana-run]
- **DISORT below absorption depth 10.** In a multi-layer beam run the fluxes below the level where the absorption
  optical depth reaches 10 are zero (`c_disort_set`, {{< code cdisort213/cdisort.c c_disort_set repo=pydisort >}});
  measured, the lost beam is at most $1.4\times10^{-6}$ and the lost reflection $1.8\times10^{-5}$ of the incident
  flux.
- **Not covered.** Scattering slabs with a closed form (the conservative semi-infinite slab, for example) are not
  among these cases; they are covered only through the benchmark of @sec-ch05-reference.
:::
